---
# TEMPLATE: package, project or tool
# Copy this whole folder into packages_projects_tools/, rename the folder, and fill in the fields below.
# See templates/README.md for step-by-step instructions and examples.
# Lines starting with # are comments - you can leave them in or delete them.

title: "Replace this with a short-ish title for the package, project or tool"

categories: # One or more topic tags, each on its own line starting with "- ".
            # Must match templates/packages_projects_tools_permitted_categories.csv exactly.
            # These are shown as tags on the entry; they don't decide where it appears on the page.
  - Replace with a category

tool-language: # Decides which section(s) of the Packages, Projects & Tools page the entry appears in.
               # Remove the # from the start of each one that applies (at least one). Must match templates/packages_projects_tools_permitted_languages.csv exactly.
  # - Python
  # - R
  # - Julia
  # - PowerBI
  # - Tableau
  # - Excel
  # - C++
  # - Desktop or Web End-user Application # e.g. a tool used through a web page or installed program, with no coding needed
  # - Meta # tools that help you do data science/OR/analytics better, e.g. GitHub, Agile methods
  # - PowerApps # C++, PowerApps, SQL, Vega and Other appear in the "Other" section
  # - SQL
  # - Vega
  # - Other

# Rating of how reusable and robust the work is - see "Choosing a rating" in templates/README.md.
# Remove the # from the start of ONE of these lines. Keep the quote marks exactly as they are.
# status: '<span style="color: #D18B12FF">Gold</span>'
# status: '<span style="color: #888888FF">Silver</span>'
# status: '<span style="color: #893400FF">Bronze</span>'

image: my_image.png # Image for the listing card and the top of the entry. Put it in this folder and give just its filename.
                    # Landscape images work best. If you don't have one, delete this line.

author: # Who made the package, project or tool. Add a "- name:" block for each author.
        # affiliation, orcid and url are optional - delete any you don't need.
  - name: Author Name
    affiliation: Their organisation or institution
    orcid: 0000-0000-0000-0000
    url: https://link-to-their-profile-or-website

date: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+00:00" # REQUIRED: when the entry was added or last updated, e.g. "2026-01-31T10:00:00+00:00".
                                  # Used to order the homepage's "Most recently added or updated" list. Don't use `today` or `last-modified`.

pub-info:
  # Icons shown after the title:
  #   - fa-hospital: significant contributions from people in the NHS, public health or other healthcare/government organisations
  #   - fa-user-graduate: significant contributions from people in academia
  # Remove the # from the start of the line that applies. If neither applies (e.g. a general-purpose tool), leave them all commented out.
  # project-type: <i class="fa-solid fa-hospital"></i>
  # project-type: <i class="fa-solid fa-user-graduate"></i>
  # project-type: <i class="fa-solid fa-hospital"></i> <i class="fa-solid fa-user-graduate"></i>

  rationale-for-status: | # Why you gave this rating. For Bronze or Silver, say what's keeping it from a higher rating.
    Replace this with the reasoning for the rating.

  entry-author: # Optional: you, the person writing this Atlas entry. Delete this block if you'd rather not be named.
    - name: Your Name
      url: https://github.com/your-username # Optional: GitHub profile, website, ORCID or similar

  abstract: | # Summary shown on the listing card and at the top of the entry. Aim for 50-200 words.
    Replace this with a short description of what the package, project or tool does, to help people decide whether to find out more.

  # Buttons shown on the listing card and the entry. Fill in the urls that apply.
  # Any link left with an empty url is hidden, so you can leave unused ones or delete them.
  # To add another, copy a block and change the name, url and icon. Icons are Font Awesome classes
  # (https://fontawesome.com/search?ic=free) - see templates/README.md for ones used elsewhere in the Atlas.
  links:
  - name: Code
    url:
    icon: fa-brands fa-github
  - name: Documentation
    url:
    icon: fa-solid fa-book
  - name: Paper
    url:
    icon: fa-solid fa-file-contract
  - name: PyPi
    url:
    icon: fa-solid fa-brands fa-python
  - name: CRAN
    url:
    icon: fa-solid fa-brands fa-r-project
  - name: Website
    url:
    icon: fa-solid fa-globe
  # - name: App
  #   url:
  #   icon: fa-solid fa-globe
  # - name: YouTube
  #   url:
  #   icon: fa-brands fa-youtube

# OPTIONAL: show a grid of related Atlas entries on this page (e.g. other entries with the same category).
# Remove the # from these lines, and from the "Related projects" section at the bottom of the page.
# listing:
#   - id: related
#     type: grid
#     grid-columns: 2
#     categories: true
#     template: "../listing.ejs"
#     sort: Title
#     include:
#       categories: "Replace with a category"
#     contents: "../*/*.qmd"
---

- where it has been used, and anything it has helped achieve
- anything people should know before using it, e.g. data it needs, or limitations
